note: Filenames can never be reused; new files are rejected on releases older than 14 days (before: any release could gain new files).
A version number can never be reused, even after unpublishing.
Versions are yanked, not replaced; deletion only within 72 h or for barely-used single-owner crates.
A version cannot be pushed twice, even after it is yanked.
The proxy and checksum database pin each version's contents; re-tagging upstream changes nothing.
Released components can never be changed or deleted.
Stable versions keep their original commit when the tag is moved upstream; dev branches stay mutable. Archives are still generated by the forge, so bytes may differ for the same commit.
pip checks each file against the sha256 the index lists for it, without needing --require-hashes.
Tarballs are checked against dist.integrity.
Cargo checks every .crate against the index's sha256 (cksum).
Bundler validates gems against the compact index's checksums.
Every module is checked against go.sum and the checksum database.
Maven 3 checks .sha1 files but only warns on mismatch by default; Maven 4 fails. The checksums come from the same server as the artifact.
Packagist publishes an empty dist.shasum for forge-hosted archives, so Composer has nothing to check; the commit in the archive URL is the only pin.
pip has no default lockfile; PEP 751 pylock.toml (2025) and tools like uv and Poetry record hashes.
package-lock.json records each package's integrity hash.
Cargo.lock records each crate's checksum.
Gemfile.lock CHECKSUMS since Bundler 2.6, opt-in (bundle lock --add-checksums).
go.sum records each module's hash.
Maven has no lockfile; third-party plugins exist.
composer.lock pins the commit, but the archive hash is empty for forge-hosted packages.
PEP 458 (TUF-signed index) is not deployed; PEP 740 attestations are not verified by pip.
Registry signatures are checked only by an explicit `npm audit signatures`.
The index is not signed; TUF signing is an open Rust project goal.
Signed-gem verification is opt-in (gem install -P MediumSecurity); signing is rarely used.
The go command checks every module against the signed sum.golang.org log by default.
Maven does not check PGP signatures; a plugin is needed.
There is nothing signed to check.
API tokens can be scoped to one project but never expire (trusted publishing tokens do).
Granular tokens only; write tokens expire after at most 90 days, classic tokens were revoked.
Tokens can be scoped by endpoint and crate, with an optional expiry.
API keys have per-action and per-gem scopes, with an optional expiry.
No publish credentials exist.
User tokens can be given an expiry; no per-namespace scoping is documented.
Nothing is uploaded; tokens only trigger re-indexing.
Wheels run no code; source distributions run their build backend.
npm 12 runs no dependency install scripts unless allowed (before: all ran).
Dependencies' build scripts and procedural macros run at build time.
Pure-Ruby gems run nothing; native extensions run extconf.rb on install.
An explicit design goal: neither fetching nor building runs dependency code.
Dependency jars are not run, but javac ran classpath annotation processors implicitly until JDK 23; build plugins run by the project's choice.
Only the root project's scripts run; dependency plugins need explicit allow-plugins (Composer 2.2+).
